Irancell gateway (5.232.0.1) also refusing connections — suggests coordinated gateway filtering across multiple operators

Electro DNS resolver unreachable — likely part of the same filtering wave affecting alternative DNS infrastructure

public_summary: Significant internet degradation detected in Iran as of 15:20 UTC on July 26, 2026. Multiple international gateways operated by TIC and major ISPs are actively blocking or refusing connections. Domestic services including Snapp and Shaparak payment gateway are also affected. Foreign platforms (Telegram, WhatsApp, Instagram, YouTube) remain accessible from our vantage point outside Iran, suggesting the filtering is targeted at specific infrastructure rather than a full shutdown.
insight: The pattern of 'connection refused' on some gateways combined with timeouts on others suggests a coordinated filtering campaign rather than random infrastructure failure — the 'refused' responses indicate active intervention at the application layer, while the timeouts suggest BGP-level blackholing or deep packet injection.
recommendation: Increase monitoring frequency to 5-minute intervals during this active filtering period. Cross-reference with IODA and OONI data to determine if this is a targeted crackdown or broader infrastructure instability. Pay particular attention to whether circumvention tools (Tor, Psiphon, Snowflake) continue to function as they may be the next target.
